utterances.speaker: PETER GALBRAITH
utterances.text: Basically all this was being channeled through Zagreb. At that time, however, Ambassador Jakovich was actually based in Vienna and he only made periodic trips into Sarajevo because of the security situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In item number 4 of this cable it says that: "In a meeting called by foreign minister Mate Granic the Ambassador was told that there had been a dramatic change in the situation in BH over the last few days and Granic wanted us to be the first to know. He said that: "The HVO had agreed to close all but three detention camps in BH, the remaining three being Rodoc, Dretelj, and Capljina." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PETER GALBRAITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The Rodoc facility being the one also known as Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: PETER GALBRAITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There's also this comment that -- the third bullet, some would call it, down: "Also reporting that the HVO had appointed," sometime around this point in September 1993, "two high-level officials to oversee the welfare of the detainees; he gave the name of Vlado Pogacic," I believe it should be Pogarcic, "as one of the two." Did you know anything about Mr. Pogarcic or is that name known to you?

utterances.speaker: PETER GALBRAITH
utterances.text: It may have been, but it's not one that I now recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm coming to the end of my examination well within, I think, the time that was allotted to the Prosecution. Do note that we have a few minutes left, but I would ask the Chamber's indulgence since I think I'll only be a few more minutes. I would like the opportunity to review my notes and conclude in the morning. But I am well within the time that we promised we would take, if that's agreeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have five minutes left. After us there's another Trial Chamber that is sitting in this same court-room, so we have to conclude within five minutes. But of course, you can continue tomorrow because you have four hours, 30 minutes, and the registrar will do the arithmetic, and he is telling me that you have used two hours and 34 minutes thus far.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think we're very well within the allotted time, and frankly I think we are very close. But it would be helpful if I could just double-check and review my notes over the evening. Thank you. Unless the Judges have additional questions, we can use the time, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While you're consulting your notes, I have a question that I'd like to ask the Ambassador. You mentioned a moment ago the existence of your opposite number in Sarajevo. Now, in order to understand what was happening on the ground, unless it touches upon Rule 70, then you're not obliged to answer, but did you have frequent contacts with him, either by telephone or in written form, regarding the situation on the ground? Because we know that the Muslims and the Croats had a common enemy, and those were the Serbs. So I was just wondering whether you had any contacts with your opposite number in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our embassies communicated very regularly by cable would how -- which is how we shared information. Most of the reporting on what was going on in Bosnia was generated -- came from the embassy in Zagreb for a lot of reasons. It was very difficult for the ambassador to Sarajevo to get there, and also much of the information could be collected from the UNPROFOR mission or by our disaster assistance relief teams, which operated out of the embassy in Zagreb and went all over Bosnia. But certainly we shared in our discussions with top leaders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for the answer. It's time to close for the day. As I said a moment ago, we'll continue the examination-in-chief tomorrow morning -- or rather, tomorrow afternoon because the Judges have a plenary meeting in the morning. So the meeting is adjourned until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
